text:
maria: Heads-up — ECC correctable error spike in eu-west-gpu-pool-4 over the last 12m. Rate jumped ~0.2 -> 5.1 cE/s. Affected nodes: 8/120 (spread across racks r3/r4). Link: https://grafana.internal/r/ecs-eu-west?panel=gpuecc
alerts-bot: [ALERT] gpu.ecc.correctable.rate high on eu-west-gpu-pool-4 (8 nodes). Severity: P3. Runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc
devin: Ugh. Are these concentrated on a small subset of cards or evenly distributed? Any Xid patterns?
maria: Mostly concentrated on 2 host chassis (r3c1, r4c2) but singles elsewhere. NVML logs show repeated: "GPU0: ecc_correctable=45 in 10m; last_xid=31" on two cards. No thermal alarms. No recent firmware changes.
emily: Quick proposal: temporary isolation threshold at 3.0 cE/s sustained for 10m per-card, with escalation to replacement if >3.0 for 30m. Otherwise mark for close monitoring. We should prefer graceful quarantine over immediate physical replace to avoid churn.
sahil: +1 on being conservative. Reminder: if we route too many requests out of eu-west during peak, cross-region egress cost + tail latency will spike. Need a priority matrix: critical models -> prefer fallback to reserve pool; best-effort -> evict earlier.
leo: I ran a dry sim yesterday with a similar distribution. Results: with 3.0 cE/s sustained 10m quarantine on 6 nodes -> projected throughput loss 1.2%, tail p99 latency +40ms, cost delta +12% (routing to us-west). Script used: `scripts/sim/ecc_quarantine_sim --nodes 120 --affected 6 --threshold 3.0`
emily: fetching per-card rates: ```curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/series?query=gpu.ecc.correctable.rate
| jq '.series[] | {host: .labels.host, rate: .samples[-1].value}' | sort -r -k2 | head -n 20``` run that and paste top 20 if you want the raw distribution.
devin: Can you run a sim with threshold 2.5 cE/s and 8 nodes affected so we can compare SLO impact? If 2.5 causes >5% throughput loss we should avoid it.
maria: Ran both. Summary attached: 2.5 cE/s @8 nodes -> throughput -3.8%, p99 +70ms, cost +20%. 3.0 cE/s @6 nodes -> throughput -1.2%, p99 +40ms, cost +12%. Full CSV: https://s3.internal/sims/ecc-2230001234-summary.csv
sahil: Sounds like 3-tier policy makes sense: 1) monitor (1-3 cE/s transient), 2) graceful quarantine (>=3 cE/s sustained 10m), 3) escalate to replace (>=3 cE/s 30m or growing Xid patterns). Schedule a canary window in low traffic hours before full rollout. :ok_hand:
emily: I'll author the runbook patch: add the priority matrix, the curl/jq diagnostics, and the quarantine automation steps (mark host degraded, cordon new workloads, run 30m validation job). Will open PR against infra/runbooks today.
devin: Approve that plan. Add explicit rollback criteria: if cross-region p99 increases >100ms or cost delta >25% within first hour, abort and revert quarantines. Also add a manual override flag for svc owners.
maria: tagging owners in the PR once it's up. Also recommend a short health-probe (synthetic inference job) to run during the 30m validation to detect subtle corruption.
leo: I'll post the sim job and logs to the PR so ops can reproduce.
emily: PR created: https://github.internal/infra/runbooks/pulls/412 — pinging @devin @sahil for review.
devin: Reviewing now. If all good, let's roll the canary tonight 01:00-03:00 UTC on a single rack (r3) and monitor.
sahil: SGTM. I'll prep capacity reservations and temporary routing rules.
emily: Great — I'll include rollback steps and the exact metric dashboards to watch. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
alerts-bot: Alert resolved (rate returned to baseline) on eu-west-gpu-pool-4 after partial routing adjustments. Note: nodes still tagged for follow-up per runbook.
